title: The Job
short: Marlowe gathers trusted contractors to escort a sealed Keystone Asset to Hush.
long: A professional but slightly ominous delivery briefing. The crate is heavy, sealed, and important, but the full truth is withheld. The party starts inside the system rather than against it.
read: Marlowe checks the route map one last time. The sealed crate waits in the carriage, stamped with enough authorization marks to make opening it feel expensive.
gm: Do not play Emeris Crown Holdings as the villain yet. They are the employer and the system. Let suspicion emerge slowly.
prompt: Fantasy corporate delivery briefing at dawn: Marlowe Fairwind reviews a route map beside a sealed glowing crate loaded into a carriage; five adventurers prepare gear; subtle corporate seals and permits; no monsters, no strixwolf, no undead.
caption: The party begins inside the system: hired, trusted, and carrying more risk than they know.
image_alt: The Job scene art for The Contract.
image_prompt_used: Fantasy corporate delivery briefing at dawn: Marlowe Fairwind reviews a route map beside a sealed glowing crate loaded into a carriage; five adventurers prepare gear; subtle corporate seals and permits; no monsters, no strixwolf, no undead. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.
long_storyboard: A professional but slightly ominous delivery briefing. The crate is heavy, sealed, and important, but the full truth is withheld. The party starts inside the system rather than against it. Run this scene as contract / ordinary frame: The party begins inside the system: hired, trusted, and carrying more risk than they know. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.
read_aloud: Marlowe checks the route map one last time. The sealed crate waits in the carriage, stamped with enough authorization marks to make opening it feel expensive.
gm_notes: Do not play Emeris Crown Holdings as the villain yet. They are the employer and the system. Let suspicion emerge slowly.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
sensory_details: coffee gone bitter in a tin cup
crate hinges humming under the morning noise
body_language: Marlowe keeps her voice even but checks the seal twice
Garrick watches the exits by habit
Varian tracks the road before anyone asks

sample_dialogue.speaker: Marlowe Fairwind
sample_dialogue.line: We are not being paid to open it. We are being paid to make sure nobody else does.

sample_dialogue.speaker: Emeris clerk
sample_dialogue.line: Routine route assurance. The form says routine, and forms are paid to be optimistic.

title: Entering Sablewood™ Logistics Preserve
short: The carriage enters an ancient forest corridor rebranded as a safe logistics route.
long: The Old Sable is immense, living, and older than any corporate label. Goldspire has put its waymarkers into the ground, but the forest refuses to feel owned.
read: The road narrows between colossal trees. Goldspire waymarkers glow at measured intervals, promising safe passage, customer delight, and limited liability.
gm: Ask one player what comforting lie a corporate sign tells travelers. Use their answer later as irony.
prompt: Horse-drawn carriage carrying five adventurers enters an immense ancient forest road lined with polished glowing Goldspire waymarkers; beautiful but uneasy, no strixwolf yet, no Bramble Union, no undead.
arc_role: Threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test
caption: The branded wilderness looks managed until the forest begins quietly disagreeing.
image_alt: Entering Sablewood™ Logistics Preserve scene art for The Logistics Incident.
image_prompt_used: Horse-drawn carriage carrying five adventurers enters an immense ancient forest road lined with polished glowing Goldspire waymarkers; beautiful but uneasy, no strixwolf yet, no Bramble Union, no undead. Do not include undead, skeletons, wraiths, Open Vale, the Custodian, or the Hanging Office. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.

Run this scene as threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test: The branded wilderness looks managed until the forest begins quietly disagreeing. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

title: The Overturned Vendor Cart
short: The party finds a vendor cart blocking the road, with spilled produce, invoices, and a useless incident placard.
long: This is the first crack in the official story. The route promised safety, but the cart is ruined, the driver is dead, and the system’s response is decorative.
read: A vendor cart lies sideways across the road. Produce and invoices spill into the mud. A polished placard blinks: INCIDENT RESPONSE EXPECTED WITHIN 3–5 BUSINESS DAYS.
gm: The placard can be a standard route-monitoring glyph, not proof that anyone meaningfully knows what happened.
prompt: Overturned vendor cart blocks branded forest logistics road; scattered produce, invoices, broken wheel, polished incident placard; adventurers arrive cautiously; no strixwolf in center, maybe only a shadow nearby; no undead.
arc_role: Threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test
caption: The overturned cart gives the party a mystery before it gives them a fight.

image_prompt_used: Overturned vendor cart blocks branded forest logistics road; scattered produce, invoices, broken wheel, polished incident placard; adventurers arrive cautiously; no strixwolf in center, maybe only a shadow nearby; no undead. Do not include undead, skeletons, wraiths, Open Vale, the Custodian, or the Hanging Office. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.
long_storyboard: This is the first crack in the official story. The route promised safety, but the cart is ruined, the driver is dead, and the system’s response is decorative. Run this scene as threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test: The overturned cart gives the party a mystery before it gives them a fight. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

title: The Strixwolf Mother
short: A strange winged wolf-owl mother guards her pups while feeding from the dead driver.
long: The obvious monster is not necessarily the killer. She is frightening, hungry, and protective. This is a moral scene disguised as a monster scene.
read: A creature steps from behind the cart: wolf-bodied, owl-faced, wings folded tight. Two pups stumble behind her. Her eyes judge whether you are danger or mercy.
gm: She is feeding on the driver but probably did not kill them. The slit throat clue points elsewhere.

title: The First Roll
short: The first action roll determines whether the strixwolf calms, retreats, snaps, or trusts.
long: This roll teaches Daggerheart and sets an early ethical tone. A compassionate party may earn a future warning. A violent party may alert the true ambushers.
read: The strixwolf lowers her head. Her feathers rise along her spine. The pups go still. What do you do?
gm: Track Strixwolf Mercy. Good treatment can pay off as warning before the Bramble Union ambush.
prompt: Close emotional encounter: one adventurer cautiously extends a hand toward protective strixwolf mother and pups; rest of party waits; tense but not violent; no Bramble Union, no undead.
arc_role: Threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test
caption: The first meaningful roll teaches that this adventure is about judgment, not just success.

title: Eyes in the Brush
short: Hidden watchers prepare to spring the trap unless the PCs spot them first.
long: This is the hinge between mystery and battle. If players noticed signs, reward them with readiness.
read: A branch cracks somewhere beyond the road. For half a breath, the forest watches back.
gm: If Strixwolf Mercy applies, her distant warning cry can grant advantage here.
prompt: Tense forest road: party realizes hidden figures watching from thorny undergrowth; carriage and sealed crate vulnerable; bramblefolk silhouettes and glints of blades; no strixwolf, no undead.
arc_role: External opposition and morally complicated conflict
caption: Eyes in the brush turn investigation into an impending tactical decision.
image_alt: Eyes in the Brush scene art for Cargo Reclaimers.
image_prompt_used: Tense forest road: party realizes hidden figures watching from thorny undergrowth; carriage and sealed crate vulnerable; bramblefolk silhouettes and glints of blades; no strixwolf, no undead. Do not include the Strixwolf Mother, strixwolf pups, wolves, owlbears, or animal companions unless explicitly requested. Do not include undead, skeletons, wraiths, Open Vale, the Custodian, or the Hanging Office. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.
long_storyboard: This is the hinge between mystery and battle. If players noticed signs, reward them with readiness. Run this scene as external opposition and morally complicated conflict: Eyes in the brush turn investigation into an impending tactical decision. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.
read_aloud: A branch cracks somewhere beyond the road. For half a breath, the forest watches back.
gm_notes: If Strixwolf Mercy applies, her distant warning cry can grant advantage here.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
body_language: Varian's ears angle before his hand moves
Garrick shifts between carriage and brush

sample_dialogue.speaker: Varian Soto
sample_dialogue.line: Three watchers. Maybe four if the quiet one is better than me.

checks.prompt: Spot the scout net before it closes.
checks.outcome: Avoid surprise or identify a negotiation angle.
checks.critical_success: Cleanly resolve: Spot the scout net before it closes. Add a concrete boon, extra clue, or improved position.
checks.success_with_hope: Success, plus the player names one helpful detail or asks one follow-up question.
checks.success_with_fear: Success, but the GM exposes a cost, ticks a countdown, or reveals a new pressure tied to Eyes in the Brush.
checks.failure_with_hope: The full goal slips, but the party still learns a useful truth or avoids the worst consequence.
checks.failure_with_fear: The GM makes a hard move that follows from the fiction and leaves the next choice visible.
checks.gm_fear_spend: Spend Fear to close the ambush net, threaten the Keystone route, or force a choice between cargo and mercy.
checks.partial: On mixed or sliding results, reveal information in layers: visible fact, actionable clue, then systemic truth.

choices_consequences.consequence: Opens a tense parley before violence.

title: Arrival at Hush
short: The party enters Hush, a real warm village inside corporate branding.
long: The tone shifts from danger to welcome. Hush is officially a Community Enclave, but locally it is home.
read: You pass the ward pillar and feel a small pop, like a bubble closing behind you. The forest quiets. Friendly voices rise ahead.
gm: Do not make Hush the joke. The branding is the joke; the people are sincere.
prompt: Carriage enters warm forest village through ward pillar with ancient runes and compliance tags; villagers wave; sponsored banners in background; genuine welcome; no strixwolf, no Bramble Union, no undead.
caption: Hush must land as a warm place with jokes inside it, not as the joke.
image_alt: Arrival at Hush scene art for Seeking a Custodian.
image_prompt_used: Carriage enters warm forest village through ward pillar with ancient runes and compliance tags; villagers wave; sponsored banners in background; genuine welcome; no strixwolf, no Bramble Union, no undead. Do not include the Strixwolf Mother, strixwolf pups, wolves, owlbears, or animal companions unless explicitly requested. No strixwolf, no Bramble Union, no combat, no undead. Focus on Hush as warm and real. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.
long_storyboard: The tone shifts from danger to welcome. Hush is officially a Community Enclave, but locally it is home. Run this scene as community stakes and emotional buy-in: Hush must land as a warm place with jokes inside it, not as the joke. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.
read_aloud: You pass the ward pillar and feel a small pop, like a bubble closing behind you. The forest quiets. Friendly voices rise ahead.
gm_notes: Do not make Hush the joke. The branding is the joke; the people are sincere.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
sensory_details: repair hammers keeping time with conversation
body_language: Locals look at the crate before they look at weapons
Children are curious but kept behind familiar adults

sample_dialogue.speaker: Lausa Standworth
sample_dialogue.line: If you brought help, welcome. If you brought trouble, at least wipe your boots.

title: Local Clues
short: Fidget, Lausa, and Halython can point the party toward the Custodian.
long: This scene lets players ask questions, be charmed by Hush, and connect the delivery to people rather than a destination.
read: Every person you meet seems to have an opinion, a custom, or a small gift to press into your hands.
gm: Use NPCs to deliver warmth, directions, and hints of dependence on the ward.
prompt: Adventurers speaking with friendly Hush locals near ward pillars and community noticeboards; warm daylight, practical kindness; no monsters, no combat.
caption: Local clues make the infrastructure failure personal and specific.
image_alt: Local Clues scene art for Seeking a Custodian.
image_prompt_used: Adventurers speaking with friendly Hush locals near ward pillars and community noticeboards; warm daylight, practical kindness; no monsters, no combat. Do not include the Strixwolf Mother, strixwolf pups, wolves, owlbears, or animal companions unless explicitly requested. No strixwolf, no Bramble Union, no combat, no undead. Focus on Hush as warm and real. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.
long_storyboard: This scene lets players ask questions, be charmed by Hush, and connect the delivery to people rather than a destination. Run this scene as community stakes and emotional buy-in: Local clues make the infrastructure failure personal and specific. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.
read_aloud: Every person you meet seems to have an opinion, a custom, or a small gift to press into your hands.
gm_notes: Use NPCs to deliver warmth, directions, and hints of dependence on the ward.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.

Halython answers direct questions and ignores corporate phrasing

title: The Clover Co-op

title: The Hanging Office Exterior
short: The Custodian’s suspended treehouse-office hangs from an ancient tree.
long: This is a problem-solving scene and a visual thesis: bureaucracy has literally been hung from a living forest.
read: A cabin-sized boulder rests below the tree, tied by thick rope to a hanging office above. It blinks with inspection seals and an old warning light.
gm: Let them solve how to get attention. The tree gently stops reckless climbing.
prompt: Strange hanging treehouse-office suspended from ancient tree by ropes and pulleys, huge rune-marked counterweight boulder, inspection seals, dangling forms; adventurers stand below; no strixwolf, no undead.
caption: The Hanging Office is absurd because the system is absurd; the people inside are not.
image_alt: The Hanging Office Exterior scene art for The Hanging Office.
image_prompt_used: Strange hanging treehouse-office suspended from ancient tree by ropes and pulleys, huge rune-marked counterweight boulder, inspection seals, dangling forms; adventurers stand below; no strixwolf, no undead. Do not include the Strixwolf Mother, strixwolf pups, wolves, owlbears, or animal companions unless explicitly requested. No strixwolf, no Bramble Union, no undead. Focus on the Custodian and the Keystone Asset reveal. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.
long_storyboard: This is a problem-solving scene and a visual thesis: bureaucracy has literally been hung from a living forest. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

title: Short Rest Before the Storm
short: The party takes a short rest while the Custodian prepares the ritual.
long: This is the breath before the ordeal. Let characters tend wounds, prepare, or share one quiet line.
read: For a little while, the Old Sable gives you room to breathe.
gm: Ask each player how they prepare. Give them ownership of the battlefield.
prompt: Adventurers resting around ritual clearing: repairing armor, tending wounds, checking weapons, while Custodian prepares runes around Keystone Asset; ominous calm; no monsters yet.
caption: The short rest is a pressure valve, not dead air.
image_alt: Short Rest Before the Storm scene art for The Ward Renewal.
image_prompt_used: Adventurers resting around ritual clearing: repairing armor, tending wounds, checking weapons, while Custodian prepares runes around Keystone Asset; ominous calm; no monsters yet. Do not include the Strixwolf Mother, strixwolf pups, wolves, owlbears, or animal companions unless explicitly requested. No Strixwolf. No Bramble Union. Only Legacy Security Skeletons and Soul-Audit Wraiths as threats. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.

title: Legacy Security Skeletons
short: Old ward-security remnants rise with rusted swords.
long: They are not random undead. They are obsolete security protocols made bone and rust.
read: Four skeletons tear upward from the soil, rusted swords raised like policies nobody remembered to cancel.
gm: Use them to teach group attacks and countdown progress.
prompt: Rusted skeleton warriors claw up from ritual clearing, old security sigils hanging from bones; party braces around Custodian and Keystone Asset; no strixwolf, no Bramble Union.
caption: Legacy Security Skeletons are old protection logic with the people scraped out.
image_alt: Legacy Security Skeletons scene art for The Ward Renewal.
image_prompt_used: Rusted skeleton warriors claw up from ritual clearing, old security sigils hanging from bones; party braces around Custodian and Keystone Asset; no strixwolf, no Bramble Union. Do not include the Strixwolf Mother, strixwolf pups, wolves, owlbears, or animal companions unless explicitly requested. No Strixwolf. No Bramble Union. Only Legacy Security Skeletons and Soul-Audit Wraiths as threats. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.
long_storyboard: They are not random undead. They are obsolete security protocols made bone and rust. Run this scene as ordeal, ritual defense, and restoration: Legacy Security Skeletons are old protection logic with the people scraped out. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.
read_aloud: Four skeletons tear upward from the soil, rusted swords raised like policies nobody remembered to cancel.
gm_notes: Use them to teach group attacks and countdown progress.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
body_language: Skeletons ignore insults and react to custody claims
Garrick recognizes the stance before he admits it

sample_dialogue.speaker: Legacy Security echo
sample_dialogue.line: Asset protection priority supersedes resident safety.

short: The countdown reaches zero and the ward renewal completes.
long: The fight ends with catharsis, not a boss death. The party protected the person doing the work.

title: The Relay Spire Hook
short: The Custodian reveals another relay spire may be failing.
long: This closes the one-shot and opens the campaign door. The system’s failure was not isolated.
read: “It’s good to have heroes in the Old Sable again.”
gm: End here. Do not over-explain the next adventure unless players ask.
prompt: Cinematic pullback above Sablewood: stone relay spires break through treeline with small flames, one distant spire burns thin; party looks toward horizon from Hanging Office; no strixwolf, no Bramble Union, no undead foreground.
caption: The Relay Spire hook points beyond the one-shot without stealing this ending.
image_alt: The Relay Spire Hook scene art for Beyond the Contract.
image_prompt_used: Cinematic pullback above Sablewood: stone relay spires break through treeline with small flames, one distant spire burns thin; party looks toward horizon from Hanging Office; no strixwolf, no Bramble Union, no undead foreground. Do not include the Strixwolf Mother, strixwolf pups, wolves, owlbears, or animal companions unless explicitly requested. No strixwolf, no Bramble Union, no skeletons, no wraiths, no combat unless explicitly requested. 4:3 cinematic fantasy concept art, no visible text, no captions, no logos, no UI, no watermark.
long_storyboard: This closes the one-shot and opens the campaign door. The system’s failure was not isolated. Run this scene as return, consequence, and next hook: The Relay Spire hook points beyond the one-shot without stealing this ending. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.
read_aloud: “It’s good to have heroes in the Old Sable again.”
gm_notes: End here. Do not over-explain the next adventure unless players ask.
Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.
sensory_details: ward chimes answering out of sync
body_language: The Custodian watches the distance before saying anything
Marlowe does not pretend she failed to hear

sample_dialogue.speaker: Whitefire Custodian
sample_dialogue.line: If Open Vale was the symptom, the Relay Spire is where someone taught the fever to bill us.

checks.prompt: Understand the next problem just enough to want the next session.
checks.outcome: Frame future hook without exposition flood.
checks.critical_success: Cleanly resolve: Understand the next problem just enough to want the next session. Add a concrete boon, extra clue, or improved position.
checks.success_with_hope: Success, plus the player names one helpful detail or asks one follow-up question.
checks.success_with_fear: Success, but the GM exposes a cost, ticks a countdown, or reveals a new pressure tied to The Relay Spire Hook.
checks.failure_with_hope: The full goal slips, but the party still learns a useful truth or avoids the worst consequence.
checks.failure_with_fear: The GM makes a hard move that follows from the fiction and leaves the next choice visible.
checks.gm_fear_spend: Spend Fear to complicate the report, sharpen the relay hook, or show how the system edits a victory.
checks.partial: On mixed or sliding results, reveal information in layers: visible fact, actionable clue, then systemic truth.

choices_consequences.payoff: The hook remains in the world.

official_results.failure_with_hope: Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
official_results.failure_with_fear: Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.

bands.botch: The wrong report protects the stack more than Hush. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
bands.miss: The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
bands.hit: The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
bands.clean: The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
bands.soar: The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: Lion-Sealed Writ.
bands.crit: Best case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.

roll_cards.slider_label: Kyle Slider / house adjudication style; overlay only, not official Daggerheart.
roll_cards.hope_spin: Gain Hope. If using the Slider overlay, soften the band cost by one notch when it fits the fiction.
roll_cards.fear_spin: GM gains Fear. If using the optional P2P Jenga variant, pull a tower block only when Kyle enabled that mode.
gm_fear_spends: Advance a visible timer or move a threat into better position.
Reveal an omitted clause, route cost, ward symptom, or human consequence.
class_community_ancestry_reveals: Every PC should name one truth they refuse to lose.
roll_cards.duality_text: Roll Hope and Fear d12s, add the chosen trait, compare to the hinge, then read the higher die for Hope/Fear spin.
roll_cards.jenga_text: Optional P2P Jenga Fear Variant, off by default and not official Daggerheart: roll one Hope d12 and use the tower for Fear only if Kyle enables it.

conditions_hazards: No official condition unless a feature, hazard, or fictional position calls for Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable.
search_loot_clues: No fixed loot. Offer clue, texture, or hospitality only when the fiction supports it.
no_roll_guidance: Do not call for a roll when the players have time, a clear method, and no meaningful pressure.
tv_mechanics_caption: Public cue: The Relay Spire Hook asks what the party does, what it costs, and who is protected.
trait_variety_note: Primary traits in this scene: Instinct, Knowledge, Presence. If rolls drift toward Instinct/Presence, ask whether Agility, Strength, Finesse, or Knowledge better describes the action.
